newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt considers confidence vote over decree.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt considers confidence vote over decree.

text.p: The Italian government might call a parliamentary vote of confidence to ensure passage into law of a cabinet decree covering development projects, a senior politician said on Tuesday after a meeting of coalition allies.
Ratification of the decree, which will release funds for the re-development of industrial sites in Milan and Naples, has been threatened by filibustering tactics from opposition parties.

"We are evaluating whether or not to call a (confidence) vote," said Oliveiero Diliberto, parliamentary party leader of the hard-left Communist Refoundation party. "We've got to see what the opposition's position is," he added.

The decree is due to expire on November 20 unless it has been passed into law by then. It cannot be resubmitted as a result of a recent Constitutional Court ruling banning the practice of successive cabinets of re-issuing expiring decrees.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi has so far called two confidence motions during his six months in office. Victory in the votes ensures the legislation in question passes while defeat brings down the government.
Prodi does not enjoy a majority in the lower house of parliament but is supported by the Communist Refoundation party.
The centre-left government won its last confidence vote last week, over a decree on troubled Banco di Napoli.
